title: A committee of the rule, the student and GLiNER, weighted by dev accuracy and examined once on a fresh sealed set: it passes where its student passes and never beats its best member
request: Phase 7 (the owner): a student behind every choice; 29.16 lets a point be answered by a vote of the rule, its student, GLiNER and a model role, each weighted by its measured accuracy, examined like any student, Claude voting only in evaluation.
plan: A pure vote in dclab_core: a weight per member from its accuracy, the heaviest option, ties to the heaviest member; the committee an answerer with a versioned fingerprint.
Weights measured on the v1 dev rows and written with the gate before any sealed row is read.
A fresh invented set for the exam, since the v1 sealed sets were spent by the students' exams; GLiNER asked its sealed rows; one read per point, every answerer judged by the same gate.
Claude in a second committee, on a capped sample, for evaluation only.

decisions.decision: The weight is log((k-1)a/(1-a)), zero at chance, an accuracy of 1.0 read as 0.995.
decisions.why: The weighted majority's weight when wrong options are equally likely: a member no better than chance never votes, and a member always right on finitely many rows is heavy but never infinite.

decisions.decision: A fresh set of twelve new seeds, not the v1 sealed rows.
decisions.why: Each v1 sealed set was read once by its student's exam (DMG-001 to DMG-006): a sealed set is read once, under any gate.

decisions.decision: The committee's pass is decision_gate_v1's, the same as a student's; the difference from the best member is reported, not a criterion.
decisions.why: Examined like any student, by a gate fixed before; a new criterion written now would be chosen knowing the members' dev scores.

decisions.decision: Claude only in a second committee, scored on a seeded sample.
decisions.why: The owner's rule: Claude's answers evaluate and never become homework where the truth is known by construction.
On the fresh sealed set the committee equals its student on three points and falls below the best member on three: the members' errors are shared, so a vote adds nothing.

change: dclab_core/committee.py (weight, vote, fingerprint, Committee; 0.87.0); dclab_rnd/committee.py (plan, exam, the Claude arm, their guards); decisions_gen.build(first=) and --first; the lake answers' source committee; the fresh set generated_v1_committee (its manifest committed); evidence/campaigns/committee_v1 (manifest, CMT-001 to CMT-007); the register's committee per point and the Students page's line.

findings.defect: The committee never beat its best member.
findings.scenario: CMT-001 to CMT-006: equal to the student on codes, roles and leaks; 0.0044 and 0.0059 below the perfect rule on groups and identifiers; 0.0309 below the student on time.
findings.cause: The rule and GLiNER are wrong on the same time columns, and together they outweigh the student.
findings.fix: Reported as the result; the committee not adopted.

findings.defect: The register showed a committee verdict beside a student that did not sit it.
findings.scenario: A refit student would still show the examined committee's pass.
findings.cause: The register attached the committee by point without comparing the student version it held.
findings.fix: Shown only while the committee holds the registered student.

findings.defect: Weights could be rewritten after a sealed read.
findings.scenario: The Claude arm printed every member's sealed accuracy on a sample, then plan --write could change the weights before exam.
findings.cause: write_plan overwrote the manifest at any time; the Claude arm had no spent check and could run first.
findings.fix: write_plan refused once any result exists; the Claude arm only after its point's exam and once per point and seed; each new result names the plan's hash.

findings.defect: An exam could spend its set on a committee short of a member.
findings.scenario: exam before GLiNER answered the fresh sealed rows: a two-member committee examined, the set spent.
findings.cause: A missing captured answer was an abstention.
findings.fix: Refused, before anything is written, while a member with a weight lacks any sealed answer.

findings.defect: The texts said more than the numbers.
findings.scenario: GLiNER's role weight called near zero (1.03 against 4.29); the Claude arm's 6 failed requests and its spend were not said.
findings.fix: The plan's status says both; the Claude document written before the guards records neither, and the plan says so.

findings.defect: The tie test was not a tie, and the Claude arm and the register were untested.
findings.scenario: 1.0 against 1.001; nothing checked eval_only or a repeat.
findings.cause: Tests written for the vote only.
findings.fix: A real tie (2.0 each) going to the heaviest member; the Claude arm's eval_only answers, its order and its repeat refused; the register's version check.

findings.defect: The Claude arm could pay twice for one sample.
findings.scenario: A later point's refusal, after an earlier point's answers were kept and before any result: a rerun asked and paid again.
findings.cause: Each point was checked inside the loop of requests, and the repeat guard read only result documents.
findings.fix: Every point checked and its sample drawn before the first request; kept answers with the same seed refuse a rerun.

measurements.name: CMT-001 to CMT-006, the committee's sealed exams
measurements.gate: committee_gate_v1: the committee passes decision_gate_v1 on a point as a student must; every member judged on the same decisions
measurements.result: pass on column.semantic_role (0.9483) and feature.leakage_suspect (0.9706), as their students; fail on the other four
measurements.against_gate: The gate judged each point: the committee passed on two of six; the Done when asks for the six verdicts, which exist.
limits: Invented tables of the same ten bases as v1.
The weights from v1 dev rows; GLiNER's from the rows it answered.

measurements.name: CMT-007, Claude on a fair sample
measurements.result: 360 sealed decisions, 60 a point, 6 requests failed: Claude 0.78 to 0.92 by point, the committee with Claude at or below the committee on every point

outcome: The committee is built, examined once and shown in the register; on these points it adds nothing over its student, so the students stay alone.
lessons: A vote helps only where members fail on different cases: measure how often their errors coincide before weighting them.
Every artefact that can show a sealed score is a read: order and count those reads like the exam itself.
risks: CMT-001 to CMT-007 were written before the plan's hash was recorded in each result.
